entry.title: How to find a Large Animal Bone in Crimson Desert
entry.summary:
The Large Animal Bone is one of those few crucial items you're going to need in Crimson Desert once you're into the late game. It's required to upgrade the quality of your equipment, and you'll need a significant amount (depending on how many items you want to upgrade).
This guide will help you figure out the best farming method for obtaining Large Animal Bones.
Table of contents How to get Large Animal Bones in Crimson Desert Best farming methods to get Large Animal Bone in Crimson Desert
How to get Large Animal Bones in Crimson Desert
To find Large Animal Bones, you'll need to hunt down some specific animals. You'll specifically want to target the big-bodied animals that roam around Pywel. Bears, moose, elephants, rhinos, and boars.
The basic method is pretty simple. You have to target these animals when you encounter them in the wild. The locations are random, but there are certain factors in play. If you want to find moose, you can try the mountain ranges in Pailune. Similarly, the forest areas are great for finding boars that commonly roam around. Elephants are common the Crimson Desert location as they can be found in the sandy areas.
Image via Pearl Abyss
Best farming methods to get Large Animal Bone in Crimson Desert
Out of all large animals, the moose appears to be the most common. While you'll first need to unlock Pailune, moose is the safest way to get Large Animal Bone. Another early alternative is to hunt bears, which can be found in Hernand Highlands.
Image via Pearl Abyss
Unlike the moose, a bear will attack you. If you're not careful, you can easily die. Once the animal has been defeated, press E to remove its skin. You will then find all the available resources. Large animals usually provide multiple items, including Thick Meat and Hide, which are pretty useful as crafting items.

entry.title: "Keeping teams together doesn't seem to matter to people, but for us it did": Star Wars Zero Company's director on what the industry can learn from XCOM 2
entry.summary: It seems that every week we're reporting on news of another wave of layoffs at a big game studio. In March alone, we saw 1000 staff let go at Epic Games, 124 at Eidos Montreal, and over 100 at Ubisoft's Red Storm Entertainment. And those are just the ones I can name without needing to rack my brain. In some cases, these "reorganisations" are to keep investors happy, in others they're painted as necessary for a studio to keep the lights on until its next paycheck. But every time a team loses members, they lose something that can't be replaced if the money ever begins to flow again. The shorthand and trust that develops between staff who work together for a long time, the institutional knowledge of what's been tried in the past and worked (or didn't), these only come from teams that remain intact. Many have sung the praises of institutional knowledge and holding a team together before, but in the wake of layoffs like we're seeing at the moment, it seems worth providing an example of why letting a team mature together makes for better games. entry.title: How to disarm mines during Locked Gate in ARC Raiders
entry.summary:
The Locked Gate event in ARC Raiders has always been tricky, and now it's even harder. The Week 23 trials involve disarming several mines while the event is live, which is a completely new activity with the Shrouded Skies update.
So, let's look at how you can do the needful without blowing yourself up. For starters, I advise rolling in with a free loadout. Things can go wrong quite easily, so it's best not to risk your valuable items.
How to disarm mines in ARC Raiders
Firstly, you'll need to wait for the Locked Gate event to appear in rotation. The event exclusively takes place on the Blue Gate map, so this task is quite specific. Next, head to any of the following areas.
Reinforced Reception
Raider's Refuge
Ancient Fort
Pilgrim's Peak
All these places are named POIs, so finding them isn't that difficult. Either way, I have marked the locations on the image below to make things easier. So far, I haven't found mines in any other locations or maps for that matter.
Screenshot and remix by Destructoid
You'll find several active mines spread all around these spots. You'll have to get pretty close to figure out if the area you're in is the active one. Hence, press the Ctrl button to crouch and walk slowly. That way, you can get close to the mines without triggering them.
Once you're close to a mine, you'll get the prompt to "disarm" it. Interact with the mine (when the prompt is available), and you'll defuse the explosive. Repeat until you have three stars on the task.
Image via Embark
If you find a mine but the prompt doesn't appear, it means that another player has already diffused it, so you'll have to keep searching. Just make sure that the Locked Gate event is active for the mines to appear on the map.

Protože je už po aprílu, můžou strahováci opět zveřejnit program další Virtuální Bastlírny, aniž by připravená témata působila dojmem, že jde o žert. Co mají bastlíři tento měsíc na srdci? Pravděpodobně by nás musel zasáhnout meteorit a výpadek internetu, aby Petr P. nezmínil KiCAD 10. A pro emulátory disket Gotek vznikl open-source firmware. Co ale hardware?
Do bastlířských doupat už se blíží dostupné metody pro recyklaci filamentů, v Česku je nový superrychlý výrobce plošňáků, Ikea už prodává Matter zásuvky a ve volné přírodě se již vyskytly pokusy o použití x86 motherboardů jako PCI-E breakout boardů pro Raspberry Pi. Čímž se pomalu blíží bizarnosti!
Nevěřící zraky padnou na rtuťové kabely, průšovský aprílový žertík nebo třeba kuličkový šroub bez kuliček.
Příští Virtuální Bastlírna se pod taktovkou projektu MacGyver studentského klubu SiliconHill bude konat v úterý 7. dubna od 20:00 minimálně do 22:00 (ale obvykle končí o dost později). Odkaz na konferenci se před samotnou akcí objeví na bastlířské wiki.

entry.title: How to craft and use the Water Wheel in Rust
entry.summary:
The start of the Spring Clean update in Rust brings the Water Wheel as a new deployable for players, and it's an immensely useful item. You can use it to generate electricity and power devices that require that energy source.
Let's find out how you can add this power source to your base and make it functional.
Table of contents How to get the Water Wheel in Rust How to use the Water Wheel in Rust
How to get the Water Wheel in Rust
The Water Wheel is a tier-1 item that needs to be crafted with the correct resource. You'll first need to get its blueprint, which can be obtained from multiple sources. I received it as a random loot, and you should look into elite-grade and military crates to raise the chances in your favor.
Image via Facepunch Studios
Once you find the blueprint, you can then craft the item at a level 1 Workbench. You'll need the following resources.
500 Wood
1 Sheet Metal
2 Gears
How to use the Water Wheel in Rust
The first task is to place the Water Wheel at a suitable location. The item, as you might have guessed, requires a water supply to work. Hence, you have to place it in a body of water so it gets submerged. Once the Water Wheel has been placed, it will activate and generate power.
Once the power is generated, use Root Combiners to channel it into a single source. Next, you have to place a battery based on your needs. The battery must be connected to the Root Combiner to store power.
Finally, you'll need to install Electrical Branches and Splitters to distribute the produced power. You can now add electronic devices to your base, and they will be operational (as long as you're not going over the total capacity).

entry.summary:
Alec's Request is one of the several Greymane faction quests you can complete in Crimson Desert, and it involves catching a Leopard Perch. This is one of the more beginner-friendly tasks that can be unlocked pretty early in the game.
Crimson Desert Alec's Request quest walkthrough
Once you have unlocked your Greymane camp after Chapter 3, you can begin this quest. To begin the quest, you need to speak with Alex near the forge. He will tell you about a mistake he made in not letting Ronnie cook/grill fish using the same forge. You'll ideally need a fishing pole to catch the fish. However, you can also attempt with your hand. You'll find Perches in the shallow water, but it's not guaranteed. If you're lucky, you could end up catching the fish in your first attempt.

Once you catch the fish, make sure to add it to your inventory. If you lose/sell the item, the quest will get stuck in a bug, and it will remain incomplete forever. Take the fish safely back to the camp and speak once again with Alec at the forge.
You'll then hand over the fish to him, which completes the quest. Not only do you get a few rewards for your efforts, but you also get +50 trust with the NPC.

There is a tiny wild sun trapped inside my crystal tower. I hear its garbled voice and catch the yellow of its fire through the blinding white blocks of the summit. The tower itself is so bright on the outside you can barely identify objects placed on it, but I have smashed the crust and dug a network of passages, and it’s shadier within. A realm of shining fog, slick as tooth enamel, with fissured, fugitive reflections that call to mind the beautiful quartz spacecraft in Noctis.
The relative gloom inside the tower implies that the structure’s external radiance is also a reflection. It appears to be caught in the glare of some celestial body, but if such a body exists, it emits radiation invisible to the naked eye, discernable only from its impact on other bodies. The skies of Lucid Blocks are dark and cloudy even by day, inasmuch as ‘day’ means anything in the game. There is one major astral feature, a hazy torus that neither rises nor sets, luminous enough to orient by when exploring the game's procedurally generated landscapes, but not enough to actually light your steps after dark. The only real sun here is the one below. The one I crafted. It slurs and shouts, nosing the walls of its prison.

entry.title: "I think it’s unfair to kind of geofence the genre": Original Stalker designer talks Eurojank in not-so-Euro games
entry.summary:
Video games, or more so the people who play them, I suppose, have this annoying thing where they assign a genre name as an insult. I don't want to reignite the discourse around JRPG as a term, but it certainly was used in quite a derisive and othering manner in its earlier years. The term walking sim was used more as a point of ironic degradation, even though it was perfectly apt in many ways. Then there's Eurojank, a sort of real but not technically real genre that describes ambitious but imperfect games made by European developers. entry.title: Island city-builder Nova Roma is out now, and I'd have drowned all my Romans already if it weren't for those pesky gods
entry.summary:
I have two dreams as mayor of an island town in Nova Roma, the new early access city-building game from Lion Shield and Hooded Horse. One is to erect a fantastic water network for my people - a sturdy yet poetic lattice of aqueducts, following their deft gradations down from the mountain rivers to cisterns gracefully spaced amid the insulae, forums, circuses and temples. In my reborn Rome, no populous bathhouse, tinkling fountain, or humble latrine shall ever run dry. With my other hand, I shall raise mighty dams, diverting the rivers away from my walls to avoid flooding in times of heavy rainfall, while exposing velvety expanses of buildable, tillable soil.
My citizens will learn to treat water frivolously, swilling and pissing it away in their decadence, much as they did in the Rome of old. The fools! For when my empire of hydration is complete, I will ascend the slopes and whimsically commission one final dam. Trusting in my stewardship – for what reason have I given them to disobey? - the citizens shall toil day and night to finish the structure. Then, when the last stone is laid and the sluices slam shut, they shall gaze in horror as a tidal wave engulfs their fair metropolis and sweeps all their precious bloody bathhouses away.

entry.summary: Italy’s "Piracy Shield" was designed to stop pirated live sports streams in 30 minutes, but Cloudflare says the "black box" system also puts the open Internet at risk. The American company was fined €14 million by Italian regulator AGCOM in january, for refusing to filter through its 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver. This week, Cloudflare announced that it formally appealed the fine while it continues to challenge the legality of the Piracy Shield system. entry.title: Audio recenze: Spasitel [Project Hail Mary] - 60 %
entry.summary: Výborně, místy až geniálně režírovaný film. Ale s velmi slabým scénářem. Záplava hardcore vědeckých problémů se střídá s okamžiky, kdy se ignorují nejzákladnější fyzikální zákony a elementární logika. Chvíli "Příchozí", chvíli "Galaxy Quest". Není jasné, kdy v ději uplynul den a kdy rok. Mezi spoustou humoru téměř zaniká skutečnost, že se hraje o přežití nejméně jedné civilizace. Při "Lego Movie" nebo animovaném "Spider-Manovi" jsem se několikrát dojal. Při "Spasiteli" ani na sekundu, i když to tvůrci zjevně chtěli. Bohužel jsem nečetl knihu, takže netuším, jestli za to může Andy Weir nebo Drew Goddard. (Ilča 50 %)
